**Aarhusklyngen** is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] in Denmark. It is one of the local organizational units evaluated in the national clinical quality databases and reports for [[atrieflimren]] (AFDK), published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut. The cluster's performance is closely monitored to ensure adherence to national treatment guidelines and to benchmark regional variations in cardiovascular care.

Aarhusklyngen is notable for meeting the national standard for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy in newly diagnosed patients, achieving a compliance rate of 92.4% [^src1]. The cluster is systematically evaluated across a wide range of clinical quality indicators in the 2024 and 2025 AFDK reports. These metrics include 1-year, 2-year, and 5-year anticoagulation treatment coverage [^src2], the incidence of ischemic stroke (apoplexy) [^src4], annual P-creatinine measurements for patients on DOACs [^src4], and severe outcomes such as serious bleeding [^src6], heart failure [^src7], and mortality [^src5]. 

Furthermore, Aarhusklyngen is included in national geographic distribution maps detailing the incidence of stroke among atrial fibrillation patients at the health cluster level, specifically tracked under [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] [^src4]. By providing granular, local-level data, Aarhusklyngen contributes to the hierarchical quality improvement strategy in the Danish healthcare system, allowing for targeted clinical interventions and political governance of cardiovascular treatment standards.
